checks.description: Pharmacy claims with a missing or zero days_supply
checks.business_impact: PDC adherence (M06) treats these rows as zero days of coverage, understating adherence and weakening the support-programme business case.
checks.remediation: Impute days_supply from quantity x standard pack size for the 11 highest-volume molecules; escalate the residual to the PBM vendor as a contractual data-quality defect.

checks.description: Medical claims dated in the future
checks.business_impact: Future-dated claims inflate the most recent periods of every trend, which is precisely the window launch leadership reads first.
checks.remediation: Add a hard ingestion reject for service_date > ingest_date and quarantine the affected rows for vendor replay.

checks.description: Eosinophil counts implausible for 10^9/L (likely submitted in cells/uL)
checks.business_impact: Type 2 biomarker phenotyping silently mis-classifies these patients as eosinophilic, corrupting any biomarker-defined sub-cohort.
checks.remediation: Apply a UCUM unit-harmonisation rule at ingestion and back-convert values above 20 by dividing by 1000.

checks.description: Encounters for dermatology patients with no EASI severity score
checks.business_impact: Severity-stratified effectiveness analyses can only be run on the minority of encounters that carry a score, and that minority skews to specialist care.
checks.remediation: Negotiate structured EASI capture in the next EHR network contract cycle; in the interim derive proxy severity from treatment intensity and document the proxy in the dictionary.

checks.description: Worst publication lag across contracted sources against the 30-day SLA
checks.business_impact: Any metric that depends on the QC provincial feed is structurally two months stale, so QC cannot be compared like-for-like against other provinces in a monthly review.
checks.remediation: Either re-contract for a 30-day feed or publish QC on a separate, explicitly lagged panel. Do not blend silently.

checks.business_impact: Duplicates inflate utilisation and cost metrics (M08, M11), which are the two numbers the payer dossier rests on.
checks.remediation: Add a deterministic dedupe on the natural key (patient_id, service_date, proc_code, paid_amount) in the silver layer, and assert uniqueness in the pipeline tests.

checks.description: Patient rows whose source-native sex coding is outside the M/F/U value set
checks.business_impact: Any analyst who reaches for sex_raw instead of the harmonised sex column silently drops or mis-buckets every patient sourced from the QC provincial feed.
checks.remediation: Harmonisation already exists in the `sex` column. Revoke read access to sex_raw outside the engineering role and mark it deprecated in the data dictionary.

checks.description: Registry rural share relative to the rural share of the patient spine
checks.business_impact: The registry systematically under-represents rural patients. Any PRO or quality-of-life finding drawn from it describes urban patients and must not be generalised.
checks.remediation: Either weight registry analyses to the claims spine by rurality and severity, or restrict registry-derived claims to urban populations in the label. Weighting is preferred.

checks.description: Claims dated before the patient's year of birth
checks.business_impact: A temporally impossible record anywhere in the asset undermines confidence in every date-based metric, which is most of the product.
checks.remediation: Add a cross-entity plausibility assertion (service_date >= date_of_birth) to the pipeline test suite.

checks.description: Claims referencing a provider_id absent from the provider dimension
checks.business_impact: Specialty-based analyses (M07, field targeting) silently drop these claims, biasing specialist involvement downward.
checks.remediation: Backfill the provider dimension from the full national registry rather than the active-prescriber subset.

checks.description: Patients on the spine linkable to at least one pharmacy claim
checks.business_impact: Unlinked patients cannot contribute to any treatment metric, so every therapy denominator is smaller than the epidemiological population it appears to describe.
checks.remediation: Review the deterministic linkage key and add a probabilistic fallback; report the linkage rate alongside every denominator.

checks.description: Patients on the spine with any EHR encounter
checks.business_impact: Clinical detail exists for a minority of the spine. Any metric requiring labs or severity scores runs on a subset that is not representative of the whole.
checks.remediation: Expand the EHR network contract, and always report EHR-derived metrics with their own coverage denominator.

checks.description: Contracted sources whose licence expires within 90 days
checks.business_impact: An insight published from an asset whose licence has lapsed is a contractual breach, and the insight has to be withdrawn from every downstream deck.
checks.remediation: Trigger the renewal workflow 120 days out; block publication from any source inside 30 days of expiry.

checks.description: Patients missing a confirmed diagnosis date or a first symptom date
checks.business_impact: Time-to-event metrics (M01, M02) silently exclude these patients, and the exclusion is not random.
checks.remediation: Extend the index-date algorithm to fall back to the earliest condition-specific claim when no confirmed code is present.

checks.description: Registry rows retained despite withdrawn consent
checks.business_impact: Processing data for a patient who has withdrawn consent is a privacy incident, reportable regardless of whether the row ever reached a report.
checks.remediation: Add a consent-withdrawal purge job on the registry refresh and enforce consent_flag = 1 in the cohort layer.

M05_persistence_12mo__rurality.label: 12-month persistence rate on advanced therapy
M05_persistence_12mo__rurality.caveat: Initiators after 2025-06-30 are excluded to avoid right-censoring bias; the denominator is therefore not the full cohort.

M05_persistence_12mo__rurality.caveat: Initiators after 2025-06-30 are excluded to avoid right-censoring bias; the denominator is therefore not the full cohort.

M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients__severity.caveat: Exposed to duplicate-claim defect DQ-06; the deduplicated figure is the governed one.

M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients__severity.label: ED visits per 100 patients
M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients__severity.caveat: Exposed to duplicate-claim defect DQ-06; the deduplicated figure is the governed one.

M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients__severity.caveat: Exposed to duplicate-claim defect DQ-06; the deduplicated figure is the governed one.

M01_time_to_diagnosis.label: Time to confirmed diagnosis
M01_time_to_diagnosis.definition: Days from the first claim carrying a Type 2 symptom code to the first claim carrying a confirmed diagnosis code. Patients with no confirmed diagnosis are excluded.
M01_time_to_diagnosis.decision_supported: Where to place disease-awareness and referral-pathway investment; sizing the diagnostic odyssey.
M01_time_to_diagnosis.caveat: Left-censored: symptoms occurring before enrolment_start are invisible, so this is a floor, not a true onset-to-diagnosis time.

M02_time_to_advanced_therapy.label: Time from diagnosis to advanced therapy
M02_time_to_advanced_therapy.definition: Days from confirmed diagnosis to the first dispensed biologic or JAK inhibitor. Only patients who initiate are included.
M02_time_to_advanced_therapy.decision_supported: Field-medical targeting; identifying where escalation is slowest relative to guidelines.
M02_time_to_advanced_therapy.caveat: Conditioned on initiation - it does not describe the patients who never escalate. Pair with M03 and M14.

M03_advanced_therapy_initiation_rate.label: Advanced therapy initiation rate
M03_advanced_therapy_initiation_rate.definition: Share of the cohort with at least one dispensed biologic or JAK inhibitor at any point in their enrolment window.
M03_advanced_therapy_initiation_rate.decision_supported: Market sizing and identification of under-treated segments.
M03_advanced_therapy_initiation_rate.caveat: Dispensing is not administration; free-goods and patient support programme volume is not visible in PBM claims.

M04_brand_share_new_starts.label: SANOVIA share of new advanced-therapy starts
M04_brand_share_new_starts.definition: Of all patients starting a biologic or JAK inhibitor in a calendar month, the share whose start is SANOVIA. Restricted to months from the September 2024 launch onward.
M04_brand_share_new_starts.decision_supported: The core launch-tracking metric: is uptake on curve?
M04_brand_share_new_starts.caveat: The two most recent months are systematically understated because of pharmacy claim run-off; never read the last bar.

M05_persistence_12mo.label: 12-month persistence rate on advanced therapy
M05_persistence_12mo.definition: Of patients who initiated advanced therapy on or before 2025-06-30, the share with at least one further advanced-therapy fill 300-390 days after their index fill.
M05_persistence_12mo.caveat: Initiators after 2025-06-30 are excluded to avoid right-censoring bias; the denominator is therefore not the full cohort.

M06_pdc_adherence.label: Proportion of days covered (PDC), first year
M06_pdc_adherence.definition: Sum of days_supply dispensed in the 365 days from index advanced-therapy fill, divided by 365 and capped at 1.0.
M06_pdc_adherence.decision_supported: Quantifying the adherence gap the support programme must close.
M06_pdc_adherence.caveat: DIRECTLY exposed to defect DQ-01. Rows with NULL/0 days_supply are treated as zero coverage, which biases PDC downward. This metric is gated Amber until DQ-01 is remediated.

M07_specialist_involvement_rate.label: Specialist involvement rate
M07_specialist_involvement_rate.definition: Share of the cohort with at least one specialist consult claim (fee code A605) at any point in their enrolment window.
M07_specialist_involvement_rate.decision_supported: Referral-pathway strategy; where GPs manage alone.
M07_specialist_involvement_rate.caveat: Fee-code capture differs between the private payer and QC provincial feeds; cross-province comparison is directional only.

M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients.label: ED visits per 100 patients
M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients.definition: Count of emergency department claims (fee code H101) divided by cohort size, expressed per 100 patients.
M08_ed_visits_per_100_patients.caveat: Exposed to duplicate-claim defect DQ-06; the deduplicated figure is the governed one.

M09_treatment_sequence.label: Most common treatment sequences
M09_treatment_sequence.definition: Ordered distinct therapeutic classes dispensed to each patient, concatenated in first-fill order.
M09_treatment_sequence.decision_supported: Where SANOVIA actually sits in the real pathway versus where the guideline says it should.
M09_treatment_sequence.caveat: Classes dispensed before enrolment_start are invisible, so sequences are truncated on the left.

M10_switch_rate_12mo.label: 12-month advanced-therapy switch rate
M10_switch_rate_12mo.definition: Share of advanced-therapy initiators dispensed a second, different advanced-therapy brand within 365 days of index.
M10_switch_rate_12mo.caveat: A dose-form change recorded under a different label would be misread as a switch.

M11_annual_cost_per_patient.label: Direct medical cost per patient-year
M11_annual_cost_per_patient.definition: Total paid amount across medical and pharmacy claims per patient, annualised over their enrolment window.
M11_annual_cost_per_patient.decision_supported: Payer value dossier and budget-impact modelling.
M11_annual_cost_per_patient.caveat: Paid amount, not list price, and excludes indirect costs and out-of-pocket spend.

M12_untreated_severe_gap.label: Severe patients with no systemic or advanced therapy
M12_untreated_severe_gap.definition: Share of patients recorded as severe who have no systemic immunosuppressant, systemic corticosteroid, biologic or JAK dispensing on record - the clinical white space.
M12_untreated_severe_gap.decision_supported: The single largest unmet-need signal for launch territory prioritisation.
M12_untreated_severe_gap.caveat: Absence of a claim is not absence of treatment - samples, hospital-supplied product and cash purchases are invisible. Treat as an upper bound on true under-treatment.

M13_quality_of_life_dlqi.label: Patient-reported quality of life (DLQI) at registry enrolment
M13_quality_of_life_dlqi.definition: Dermatology Life Quality Index (0-30, higher is worse) recorded at enrolment in the consented Type 2 registry. Rows with withdrawn consent are excluded at the cohort layer.
M13_quality_of_life_dlqi.decision_supported: The humanistic-burden chapter of the payer dossier and the patient-voice narrative for launch.
M13_quality_of_life_dlqi.caveat: The registry is a volunteer, specialist-referred, predominantly urban population. This is the single least generalisable asset in the product and is included here precisely to demonstrate the Fitness-for-Use gate refusing it.

rurality.description: Urban vs rural residence - the health-equity lens.

age_band.expr: CASE WHEN (2026 - birth_year) < 12 THEN '0-11' WHEN (2026 - birth_year) < 18 THEN '12-17' WHEN (2026 - birth_year) < 40 THEN '18-39' WHEN (2026 - birth_year) < 65 THEN '40-64' ELSE '65+' END
age_band.description: Age band as of the 2026 reference year.

patient.description: De-identified patient spine with enrollment window, geography, payer type and clinician-assigned severity.

key_columns.patient_id: Surrogate key. Never a real health card number.
key_columns.birth_year: Year only - full DOB is suppressed at ingestion.
key_columns.sex_raw: Source-native coding; QC admin source uses 1/2. Do NOT use for analysis - demonstrates the conformance defect.
key_columns.province: Two-letter province code; TERR groups the territories.
key_columns.rurality: urban | rural, derived from postal FSA (synthetic here).
key_columns.enrollment_start: First date of continuous data capture.
key_columns.enrollment_end: Last date of continuous data capture.
key_columns.first_symptom_date: First claim carrying a Type 2 symptom code.
key_columns.index_dx_date: First claim carrying a confirmed diagnosis code.

claim_medical.grain: one row per medical claim line
claim_medical.description: Adjudicated medical claims from private payer and provincial administrative sources.

key_columns.service_date: Date of service. Subject to future-date defect DQ-02.
key_columns.proc_code: Fee code. A605 = specialist consult, H101 = ED visit.
key_columns.paid_amount: Amount paid in CAD. Not list price.
key_columns.ingest_date: When the row landed in HELIOS - drives latency KPIs.

key_columns.drug_name: Brand or molecule label. SANOVIA is the fictional launch brand used throughout this demo.
key_columns.drug_class: Therapeutic class. biologic_* and jak are advanced therapy.
key_columns.days_supply: Days of therapy dispensed. NULL/0 on ~7% of rows (defect DQ-01) - materially affects PDC adherence.

ehr_encounter.description: Ambulatory EHR network - the only source with clinical severity scores and labs. Covers ~42% of the spine.

key_columns.easi_score: Eczema Area and Severity Index (0-72). ~40% missing.
key_columns.eosinophil_count: Blood eosinophils in 10^9/L. ~5% submitted in cells/uL instead (defect DQ-03).

registry_enrollment.description: Consented Type 2 inflammation patient registry. Rich PRO data but strongly selected - see DQ-08.

key_columns.consent_flag: 0 = consent withdrawn; rows MUST be excluded.

key_columns.specialty: GP | DERM | RESP | ALLERGY | PEDS | IM

source_metadata.grain: one row per contracted data source
source_metadata.description: Contract, cadence, lag, consent basis and licence expiry for each asset. Drives the timeliness and licence checks.

key_columns.license_expiry: Contract end date - insights past this cannot ship.

agent_answers.question: How long do patients wait for a confirmed diagnosis?
agent_answers.narrative:
Across 40,000 patients, the median time to confirmed diagnosis is 161 days, with an interquartile range of 104 to 243 days.

Broken out by rurality:
  - urban: 150 days (n=32,493)
  - rural: 227 days (n=7,507)

The spread is material: rural at 227 days against urban at 150 days, a ratio of 1.51x.

How to read this: Directional only. Must be published with its caveat attached and must not be the sole basis for an investment decision.
Caveat carried by this metric: Left-censored: symptoms occurring before enrolment_start are invisible, so this is a floor, not a true onset-to-diagnosis time.

agent_answers.question: Is SANOVIA uptake tracking to the launch curve?
agent_answers.narrative:
SANOVIA share of new advanced-therapy starts reached 15.5% in 2026-06, up from 12.4% in 2024-12. The series covers 22 periods and 2,143 new starts in total.
4 of the 22 periods are suppressed because the monthly count of new starts falls below the minimum cell size.

How to read this: Directional only. Must be published with its caveat attached and must not be the sole basis for an investment decision.
Caveat carried by this metric: The two most recent months are systematically understated because of pharmacy claim run-off; never read the last bar.

agent_answers.question: How many severe patients are getting no systemic therapy at all?
agent_answers.narrative:
Severe patients with no systemic or advanced therapy is 39.2% (95% CI 38.1 to 40.4), based on 2,762 of 7,044 patients.

Broken out by province:
  - ON: 38.0% [95% CI 36.2-39.9] (n=2,656)
  - QC: 37.6% [95% CI 35.2-40.0] (n=1,618)
  - BC: 39.8% [95% CI 36.8-43.0] (n=959)
  - AB: 37.4% [95% CI 34.2-40.7] (n=834)
  - MB: 47.2% [95% CI 41.1-53.4] (n=252)
  - SK: 44.8% [95% CI 38.5-51.4] (n=223)
  - NS: 41.3% [95% CI 34.4-48.7] (n=179)
  - NB: 48.4% [95% CI 40.9-56.1] (n=161)
  - NL: 48.8% [95% CI 38.6-59.2] (n=86)
  - PE: 50.0% [95% CI 33.6-66.4] (n=32)
  - TERR: 50.0% [95% CI 35.8-64.2] (n=44)

The spread is material: PE at 50.0% against AB at 37.4%, a ratio of 1.34x.

How to read this: Decision-grade. May be quoted directly in a governance forum.
Caveat carried by this metric: Absence of a claim is not absence of treatment - samples, hospital-supplied product and cash purchases are invisible. Treat as an upper bound on true under-treatment.

agent_answers.question: Does payer channel change access to advanced therapy?
agent_answers.narrative:
Advanced therapy initiation rate is 9.8% (95% CI 9.5 to 10.1), based on 3,924 of 40,000 patients.

Broken out by insurance type:
  - public: 10.0% [95% CI 9.5-10.4] (n=17,653)
  - private: 9.9% [95% CI 9.4-10.4] (n=15,057)
  - mixed: 10.3% [95% CI 9.6-11.1] (n=6,098)
  - uninsured: 3.8% [95% CI 2.8-5.0] (n=1,192)

The spread is material: mixed at 10.3% against uninsured at 3.8%, a ratio of 2.73x.

How to read this: Decision-grade. May be quoted directly in a governance forum.
Caveat carried by this metric: Dispensing is not administration; free-goods and patient support programme volume is not visible in PBM claims.

Across 1,146 patients, the median proportion of days covered (pdc), first year is 0.62, with an interquartile range of 0 to 1 proportion 0-1.

agent_answers.question: What does the real treatment pathway look like?
agent_answers.narrative:
The most common patterns across 40,000 patients are: topical_cs (42.0%, n=16,805); inhaled_controller (20.5%, n=8,196); topical_cs > topical_tci (7.4%, n=2,977).

How to read this: Directional only. Must be published with its caveat attached and must not be the sole basis for an investment decision.
Caveat carried by this metric: Classes dispensed before enrolment_start are invisible, so sequences are truncated on the left.

agent_answers.question: What is the patient reported quality of life in the registry?
agent_answers.narrative:
HELIOS cannot answer this question. The data is not fit for this particular question.

Fitness-for-Use score 36.1/100 (RED) for Patient-reported quality of life (DLQI) at registry enrolment on this cohort.

  - V1 - representativeness scores 0/100, driven by DQ-08 (Registry rural share relative to the rural share of the patient spine)
  - V1 - governance scores 0/100, driven by DQ-15 (Registry rows retained despite withdrawn consent)
  - V2/V4 - DQ-15: Registry rows retained despite withdrawn consent (55 rows)

What would have to change: Either weight registry analyses to the claims spine by rurality and severity, or restrict registry-derived claims to urban populations in the label. Weighting is preferred.

agent_answers.question: Which individual doctor prescribes the most SANOVIA?
agent_answers.narrative:
HELIOS cannot answer this question. No governed metric covers it.

This question asks HELIOS to identify an individual prescriber. The product reports on populations only; prescriber-level targeting is out of scope for this platform and is governed separately.

What would have to change: Register the question with the RWD & HI product owner. If it is a recurring decision need, it becomes a new governed metric with a definition, an owner and a DQ profile.
